item.title: Griffin’s Move Offers AI Reprieve as Traders Eye More Blowouts
item.description: Billionaire Ken Griffin’s rescue of hedge fund Situational Awareness helped trigger a relief rally in global AI stocks, leaving traders debating if the worst is over or more blowouts are on the way.

item.title: DeepSeek Unveils Public Beta API for Flagship AI Model
item.description: China’s DeepSeek rolled out a public beta application programming interface, or API, for its flagship artificial intelligence model, V4 Flash, touting advancements in agentic abilities.

item.title: French Inflation Unexpectedly Accelerates on Services, Power
item.description: French inflation unexpectedly quickened this month, supporting the case for another European Central Bank interest-rate increase.

item.title: Kioxia’s Outlook Miss Clouds Optimism About Memory Chip Boom
item.description: Kioxia Holdings Corp. issued a disappointing earnings outlook after results missed expectations, a sign that an unprecedented AI-driven surge in flash memory prices may be moderating.

item.title: Sainsbury’s to Sell Argos Division for at Least £120 Million
item.description: J Sainsbury Plc agreed to sell its struggling Argos general merchandise unit to Swift Partners, a new company backed by retailers including former Co-op boss Richard Pennycook.

item.title: BP Starts Process for Potential Sale of North Sea Business
item.description: BP Plc said it’s starting a process to market its North Sea business for a potential sale, as part of a wider review of the oil major’s portfolio.

item.title: UK House Prices Edge Higher in July, Nationwide Says
item.description: UK house prices returned to growth in July, one of the country’s largest mortgage lenders said, as buyers weather higher borrowing costs linked to the Iran war better than expected.

item.title: Tokyo Court Says Shidax Tender Undervalued the Firm in Rare Case
item.description: The Tokyo District Court ruled that hospitality sector company Shidax Corp.’s tender offer in 2023 to go private undervalued its shares, in one of the still-rare cases in Japan of financial tussles between companies getting resolved by legal authorities.

item.title: FTSE Live: UK Stock Futures Rise, Pound Slips as Attention on Tech
item.description: FTSE Live: UK Stock Futures Rise, Pound Slips as Attention on Tech【原文：FTSE Live: UK Stock Futures Rise, Pound Slips as Attention on Tech】

item.title: Engie Lifts Profit Outlook on Cost Cuts, Currency Effects
item.description: French utility Engie SA raised its full-year profit forecast as it benefits from currency fluctuations, its huge acquisition in the UK, cost cuts and energy market volatility linked to the war in the Middle East, which helped mitigate a profit decline in the first six months of the year.

item.title: Saudi Ships Pivot from Red Sea Chokepoint for Rare Africa Trip
item.description: Six Saudi oil tankers are sailing away from the Bab el-Mandeb chokepoint and appeared to be embarking on an unusual trip around Africa as threats from Houthi rebels upend shipping in the Red Sea.

item.title: Yen Strategists Parse IMF Rules for Clues to Japan’s Next Move
item.description: Strategists trying to figure out Japan’s next move on the yen are looking to the International Monetary Fund’s technical guidelines for clues.

item.title: Kenya Inflation Tops Target Midpoint a Third Month on Energy
item.description: Kenya’s annual inflation rate exceeded the midpoint of the central bank’s target range for a third month, as energy costs fueled price growth.

item.title: SNB Returns to Profit as Stocks Rally Offsets Gold Losses
item.description: The Swiss National Bank reported a solid six-month profit, as gains from the global stock-market rally and a weaker franc offset the drop in value of its gold holdings.

item.title: Sony to Begin Phased Restart of Quake-Hit Sensor Plant Tuesday
item.description: Sony Group Corp. said it will begin a phased restart of its image sensor factory in Kyushu on Tuesday, after a magnitude-7.1 quake and numerous aftershocks shook Japan’s southwestern island.

item.title: Strategists Await Ueda Guidance After BOJ’s Steady Decision
item.description: Strategists are watching out for indications of future policy at a Bank of Japan press conference later Friday as they assess yen weakness following the central bank’s decision to hold rates unchanged.

item.title: Kontrolmatik’s Rise and Fall Burns Turkey’s Retail Traders
item.description: Small-time investor Riza Gundogdu thought he had found the next Tesla Inc. early last year when he invested in shares of Kontrolmatik Enerji ve Muhendislik AS.

item.title: Copper Set for Monthly Gain on Tightening Global Supply Outlook
item.description: Copper headed for a monthly advance on growing signs of tight supply, fueled in part by large flows of material to the US ahead of a highly-anticipated decision by the Trump administration on import tariffs.

item.title: Swiggy, Eternal Stocks Surge as Zepto’s India IPO Hits Roadblock
item.description: Shares of the main competitors to Indian rapid-commerce firm Zepto Ltd. are set for their best month in years after the loss-making company’s planned initial public offering hit a roadblock.

item.title: PBOC’s Weaker Daily Fixing to Temper Yuan Gains, Analysts Say
item.description: China’s central bank set the yuan’s fixing at a weaker-than-expected level, a move that some analysts said may indicate a desire to slow the pace of gains after the currency climbed to a three-year high.

item.title: Asian Stocks Post Biggest Gain in Four Months on AI Optimism
item.description: Asian stocks posted their biggest gain in nearly four months as investors piled into chipmakers, after blockbuster earnings from major tech firms reinforced optimism over AI demand.

item.title: JPY/USD: BOJ Holds Rate Steady And Upgrades View on Economy
item.description: The Bank of Japan kept its policy settings unchanged while signaling less caution about economic growth, pointing to confidence that the economy remains on track for further policy normalization after it lifted its benchmark rate last month to the highest since 1995.

item.title: Bank of Japan Holds Interest Rate Steady at 1% as Expected
item.description: The Bank of Japan kept its policy settings unchanged at the end of its two-day meeting on Friday after lifting its benchmark rate last month to the highest since 1995.

item.title: North Korea’s Economy Expands on Russia Arms Deals, China Trade
item.description: North Korea’s economy expanded for a third straight year in 2025, boosted by arms exports to Russia, stronger trade with China, and Kim Jong Un’s drive to develop regional industries, according to estimates by South Korea’s central bank.

item.title: Philippines to Revamp Bond Pricing Ahead of JPM Index Inclusion
item.description: The Philippines plans to change the way it prices local-currency bonds by removing the impact of withholding tax, a shift that may saddle some existing investors in the nation’s $230 billion market with losses, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Nikkei Weight Cut Shadow Looms Over Advantest After 18% Rally
item.description: Advantest Corp.’s shares may come under selling pressure from passive funds as the Japanese chip-tester maker’s weighting in the Nikkei 225 Stock Average may be lowered at the next review.

item.title: Thailand’s True Internet Data Center Seeks $2 Billion Loan
item.description: Thailand’s True Internet Data Center Co. is seeking an about $2 billion-equivalent loan to build a new facility, according to people familiar with the matter, as the country looks to become a regional hub for artificial intelligence and cloud services.

item.title: Iron Ore Climbs as Traders Weigh Supply Risks From BHP Strike
item.description: Iron ore rose as threat of strike action by BHP Group workers at the export hub of Port Hedland raised concerns about potential supply disruptions, although weak Chinese demand will likely cap price gains.

item.title: Rising US Yields May Complicate RBI’s Strategy on Rates and the Rupee
item.description: If US yields keep rising, the RBI could face growing pressure to keep policy tighter.

item.title: Korea Working Closely With US, Japan After Overnight FX Jump
item.description: South Korea’s foreign-exchange authorities are in close contact with counterparts in the US and Japan, a senior finance ministry official said, a day after Tokyo mounted a large-scale operation to prop up the yen.
